text:
Jackson Blake won a Stanley Cup with Carolina last spring, and he has started the follow-up like a player who wants a bigger job. He has 19 points in 19 games, a nine-game point streak, and he's on the ice for 83% of the Hurricanes' power-play chances, up from 40% last season. Not bad for a 2021 fourth-round pick, 109th overall.

This one is built on process. At five on five, Carolina gets 65% of the expected goals (the share of chance quality) with Blake on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season, 93rd percentile among forwards once teammates and opponents are accounted for. He also plays with strong teammates, which helps; The Hockey Writers has him and Logan Stankoven "Becoming a Dangerous Duo."

If anything, the goals are behind: 5 on 7.8 expected, so his finishing has been a little unlucky even as the team has scored slightly more than its chances with him on. Our projection has him finishing the season around 67 points, in a range from 56 to 79. We'd watch the power play: that's where his role grew, and where a cold patch would show first.
headline: Jackson Blake's breakout has real roots
